$comment: The paper doll. docs/ecosystem/23-tessera.md §2.8 and §6.3.
One base plus overlays composited at render time, which is how a 2D world gets combinatorial
appearance out of 48 assets instead of thousands: 4 builds x 8^5 = 131,072 distinct avatars
before colourway. All 48 are 256x512 and therefore NON-SQUARE, so they are the largest block
of assets in this repository exposed to Qwen's transposed `size`.
REGISTRATION IS THE FAILURE THAT HIDES. Every overlay is generated against the same base
silhouette, stated in the prompt below and checked by verify.py check 8 as a bounding-box
containment test. A misregistered overlay is invisible in a contact sheet and obvious in play —
which is the definition of a check worth automating.
AND IT DID HIDE, ONCE. The first run of these 40 overlays put 32 of FLUX's and 40 of Qwen's
outside their band. The `region` strings then read like 'the head only — the top quarter of
the frame; everything below the jaw is empty': a positive half naming the part, and a NEGATIVE
half naming where the ink may not go. Both models honoured the first half and dropped the
second, identically, and when two independent models fail one instruction the same way the
instruction is the defect rather than the models.
So `region` is now positive throughout, and it is joined by two fields that say the same thing
in the two registers a diffusion model and a checker respectively understand:
band       the AIM, as a fraction of the frame's height, top and bottom. Numbers, for code.
placement  that same band as prose, because a model is asked in words and 0.8 is not a word.
`band` IS NOT THE TOLERANCE, and the difference is deliberate. verify.py's SLOT_BANDS is the
tolerance — wider, plus a margin — and it is the arbiter. These are what the prompt AIMS at,
set inside it, so a plate that lands near its aim passes with room rather than on the line.
Two numbers for two purposes is not the drift defect; one number doing both jobs would mean
either a prompt that asks for the edge of what is allowed or a check that only accepts perfection.
